title: SLO-backed minimum commit scenarios
body:
Goal: sketch defensible minimum-commit offers that are explicitly tied to latency SLOs and predictable capacity. Rapid back-of-envelope scenarios to share with PM/SE for pricing model.

Background / rationale:
- Customers who need low p95 latency (<150ms for 1k tokens) will implicitly need reserved capacity (Dedicated or Private) for predictable queuing and GPU warm KV caches.
- We want an entree-level minimum commit that caps our downside while still being attractive relative to pure PAYG.
- Two levers to play with: financial (monthly $ commit) + operational (reservation type: soft bursts vs hard guarantee).

Assumptions (pickable knobs):
- Model: trimmed gpt-large-equivalent (L = ~70B), typical unquantized GPU throughput baseline: ~120 tokens/sec on a V100-like baseline? (use 2x for Ampere/A100). For cost math use a simplified unit: "GPU-hour" price to Redwood ~ $1.00/hour (reserved amortized, after multi-tenant / committed discount). This is placeholder — confirm with infra.
- Average session: 1.2 requests / session, mean prompt+completion tokens = 800 tokens (200 prompt + 600 completion).
- Effective tokens per second per GPU (steady state, accounting for context prep): 1000 tps (optimistic A100 + batching + kv cache).
- Concurrency target to meet p95 < 150ms: < 8 requests concurrently per GPU (depends a lot on seq length). We'll assume concurrency budget C_g = 8 per GPU.
- Month = 720 hours.

Derive: sessions per GPU per month (S_g):
- If C_g = 8 concurrent requests and each request consumes average latency L_req (sec) = tokens / tps = 800 / 1000 = 0.8s (this is "service time")
- Throughput per GPU = C_g * (1 / L_req) requests/sec = 8 * (1 / 0.8) = 10 reqs/sec
- Requests per month = 10 * 3600 * 720 = 25,920,000 requests / month per GPU
- Sessions per month ~= requests per month (1:1) = 25.9M sessions

Tokens per month per GPU: 25.9M * 800 = 20.736B tokens

Cost per GPU-month (amortized reserved) = 720 * $1.00 = $720
Cost per token (reserved, fully utilized) = $720 / 20.736B = $0.0000000347 per token (~3.47e-8)

Compare to PAYG unit cost (example): $0.00003 per token (hosted high price) — huge delta. But real PAYG numbers need to be filled. The point: reserved capacity with high utilization is orders of magnitude cheaper.

Minimum-commit design patterns to sell SLO-backed offer:
1) SLO-lite: low commit, soft reservation
   - Commit: $3k/month (covers ~4 GPU-hours/day reserved buffer)
   - Operational: best-effort warm pool, allowed preemption for spikes, SLO: p95 latency < 300ms with documented caveats (e.g., 95% of days).
   - Target: SMB apps with predictable diurnal patterns; provides 1–2 GPUs worth of effective steady capacity.
   - Rough math: $3k => ~4 GPUs * $720/GPU-month ~ does not align — this is intentionally a blended credit approach (we credit bursts + PAYG). Need to clarify internal amortization.

2) SLO-standard: medium commit, explicit capacity reservation
   - Commit: $25k/month (~34 GPU-hours/day reserved after discounts) — target mid-market teams
   - Operational: dedicated capacity with soft autoscale (we guarantee baseline capacity and provide extra burst at PAYG incremental rate). SLO: p95 < 150ms for requests within baseline capacity; fallback routes for overflow.
   - Break-even calc: $25k buys ~34 GPU-hours/day => ~1.4 GPUs permanently (720 hours/month per GPU) so 34*30/720 ~1.42 GPUs effective. That single GPU (if fully utilized) can handle ~20B tokens/month per earlier calc — so this is probably undersized relative to price. This suggests we should price per-GPU-commit more than naive infra cost. Consider packaging by effective RPS or session floor instead of raw GPU hours.

3) Enterprise SLO: high commit, hard SLA
   - Commit: $150k+/month (negotiated), hard SLA with financial penalties, dedicated isolated pool (1+ GPUs pinned), priority routing, private networking.

Quick unit-econ checks to avoid gifting value:
- Effective utilization will rarely be >70% on day 1. If true utilization U = 60%, adjust reserved per-token cost by 1/U => reserved unit cost increases to ~5.8e-8 => still tiny vs PAYG but matters when size small.
- Amortized infra + ops + license + model weights + SRE margin => multiply infra baseline by 6–10x for a realistic internal cost. So treat $1/GPU-hour as bare metal; product cost to business might be $6–10/GPU-hour. Recompute: at $6/hr => GPU-month = $4320, per-token = $4320/20.736B = 2.08e-7 (~0.000000208). Still tiny but closer.

Anchoring commit by customer metrics instead of GPUs:
- Option A: commit = "min tokens per month" floor (easier for PAYG-conversion). Example: $20k/month buys 600M tokens at an effective list price of $0.000033/token — but internally we price to guarantee SLO.
- Option B: commit = "min reserved RPS" (e.g., 50 rps baseline) — maps to GPU capacity and easier to reason about latency guarantees.
- Option C: hybrid credits + seat — small seat to cover control plane and priority + credits to cover usage.

Small experiment matrix to propose to GTM / sales: (run 3 anchor offers)
- Offer 1 (SMB SLO-lite): $3k/mo commit, 50k credit monthly, p95 < 300ms best-effort, overage at PAYG *1.2 price.
- Offer 2 (Growth SLO-standard): $25k/mo commit, baseline 50 rps / 2 GPUs reserved equivalent, SLO p95 <150ms for baseline, overage routed to lower tier models or PAYG at +15% surcharge.
- Offer 3 (Enterprise SLO): $150k+ commit, isolated pool, 99.9% uptime SLA, custom billing cadence.

Questions / unknowns to resolve (action items):
- Confirm realistic tokens/sec per GPU for our actual model variants (quantized vs fp16) and average request seqlen distribution (p50/p95 lengths). Ops to run 2-week sampling job. (Action: @Devon run sample traces, link GH:infra#842)
- Confirm internal amortized GPU-hour cost (with datacenter, power, networking, ops). Finance to provide 3-tier numbers (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Model routing cost delta: how much cheaper is routing to smaller quantized model under overflow vs spinning more GPUs? Need to price fallback credit discount.
- How to communicate SLO caveats simply on SKU page (e.g., "baseline" vs "burst" definitions).

Notes / heuristics for conversations with customers:
- Use "RPS floor" for latency-critical customers; use "token floor" for price-sensitive customers.
- Emphasize operational primitives: pinned capacity, KV-cache warm, and regional placement — customers care more about predictability than raw token price.
- Offer an initial 1–3 month ramp with credits to avoid churn from mis-sizing (we can offer a 50% credit in month 1 if they sign 12-month commit).

Rough next steps:
1) Sync with infra to get empirical tps/concurrency numbers (due: 2024-11-22).
2) Ask finance for internal cost model + target margin (due: 2024-11-25).
3) Draft pricing one-pager with three SKUs and quick FAQs (due: 2024-11-29) — share with solutions eng.

Random scratch fudges / mental checks:
- If average request length jumps to 2400 tokens (long context), GPU capacity per request triples -> baseline GPUs needed x3, break-even commit must scale accordingly. Important to include a typical usage survey in the sales checklist.
- For small customers, prefer credits + soft SLA to avoid overcommitting our capacity.

End-of-note: this is intentionally rough. Main objective is to 1) produce a set of commit anchors that map to latency guarantees, 2) produce a small matrix GTM can test quickly, and 3) identify the datapoints we absolutely need from infra/finance before publishing.

— maya
